annotations.text:
E — ALMANAC, built out.

A register of record rather than a daily paper: old-style serif with oldstyle numerals, cool grey-green stock, botanical green, Roman numerals for entry numbers, double rules.

The form is entry-per-project, which is why it carries across all four screens without strain — an edition, a repo, and the alternatives directory are all registers of the same kind. That was the argument for it and it holds up.

FRONT PAGE. Masthead, beat rail, one lead entry with its measurements set as a side table, then a two-column register.

The lead blurb is longer than the rest on purpose — the editorial claim is the product, so the lead earns room to make one. Everything below it is a single specific sentence.

The headline figure is stars-a-day because that is what the data currently supports; it becomes stars-this-week once two snapshots exist a week apart.

REPO PAGE. Stats as a five-column band, then star history, then the editorial note, then the README.

The star chart is drawn as a hairline engraving with a hatched fill rather than a WebGL plot — it suits the register far better than three.js did, and it removes a 720 KB dependency from the page. Worth revisiting whether the graph needs WebGL at all.

ALTERNATIVES. One product per page, substitutes as numbered entries.

'Not yet measured' is kept visible rather than hidden — those are claims we stand behind but have not put a number to, and saying so is the honest version. 'How this list is made' stays at the foot of every one of these pages.
MOBILE. The register collapses to one column; the beat rail scrolls horizontally. Lead keeps its figure at full size — at this width the number is the thing that survives.

The six directions not taken, kept for reference.

A (Wire Service) was the leading candidate before E; C (Swiss Ledger) is the one to revisit if the register ever needs to carry dense tabular views it cannot handle.
